subject: Student-Led School Dress Code Policy Reform
overview: Andrews Middle School students and School Committee member Paul Ruseau discussed a proposed overhaul of the district's dress code policy intended to eliminate gender and racial inequities. The proposed policy shifts from a list of prohibited items to a simplified requirement for tops, bottoms, and footwear.

items.title: Project update and dress code feedback
items.summary: Students provided an update on their petition to reform the school dress code, reporting that they received a formal policy proposal from the School Committee following their initial advocacy against bans on hats and hoods.

items.title: Analysis of current policy inequities
items.summary: Students described how current dress code enforcement disproportionately targets specific body types, genders, and races, leading to inconsistent disciplinary referrals for similar clothing choices.

items.title: Subcommittee report on policy revisions
items.summary: Paul Ruseau reported on a recent subcommittee meeting where members debated gender-neutral standards and the removal of subjective language regarding "distracting" attire.

items.title: Proposed "top, bottom, and footwear" standard
items.summary: Ruseau outlined a proposed policy that replaces specific item prohibitions with a requirement for basic coverage to reduce the subjective interpretation and enforcement by individual staff members.

items.title: Implementation timeline and scope
items.summary: The School Committee is scheduled to vote on the new policy on June 6, with plans to update handbooks for a district-wide rollout in the fall semester.

items.title: Civics project origins and student impact
items.summary: Students shared how the initiative evolved from a mock legislative exercise in their civics class into a real-world policy proposal focused on student comfort and self-expression.
